paper.title_en: Majorana zero modes in half-quantum vortices of pair density wave superconductors
paper.abstract_en: Pair-density-wave (PDW) superconductors admit half-quantum vortices that can bind Majorana zero modes, but whether such defects are energetically stabilized in microscopic models remains unclear. We address this question in a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with a PDW phase. Microscopic Hartree-Fock calculations determine the superfluid stiffness $ρ$ and PDW relative-phase stiffness $κ$, and show that $κ/ρ$ approaches unity near the continuous PDW--Dirac-semimetal transition, strongly reducing the long-wavelength cost of vortex fractionalization. Combining this with microscopically extracted Ginzburg--Landau couplings, we show that vortex-core energetics favor fractionalization, producing a strongly enhanced splitting scale and a field-driven full-vortex--to--half-vortex lattice transition. We determine the resulting two-flavor half-vortex lattice structure and construct the associated Majorana lattice. Majorana hybridization produces geometry- and flux-dependent bands with Dirac nodes and zero-energy Fermi lines. Together, these results establish a microscopic route from PDW superconductivity to field-induced half-vortex and Majorana lattices.
